I give up. I did not change `/work/putnam_2016_b4.lean`, so it still contains the original `sorry`.

The statement is true, and I checked the n = 1 case by hand. The 2×2 difference A − Aᵀ has determinant d², where d = a₁₂ − a₂₁ takes values −1, 0, 1 with probabilities 1/4, 1/2, 1/4. So E[det] = 1/2, which matches (2n)!/(4ⁿ·n!) = 2!/4 = 1/2. There is no formalization loophole I can exploit.

The general case needs a real proof that I can't finish here:

- The determinant of a skew-symmetric matrix is the square of its Pfaffian, and Mathlib does not have Pfaffians.
- Averaging over all 2^(4n²) matrices requires a combinatorial argument, which I would have to build from scratch in Lean. That means expanding det(B) over permutations, identifying which terms survive expectation (the pair-matching structure), and counting the matchings to get (2n−1)!!/2ⁿ = (2n)!/(4ⁿ·n!).
- I would also need to handle the `tsum` over the subtype and the `ncard` of the set, which is doable but adds more work.

Realistically this is a multi-thousand-line formalization effort, well beyond what I can complete in this session.
